question.problem: Given that $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{3}+{z}^{4},$ find $\frac{∂f}{∂r},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $f(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂r} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂r}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂r}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂r} \\  & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{∂f}{∂y}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2x,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta , \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =3{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂r} & =(2r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +(3{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2r{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +3{r}^{2}{sin}^{3}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
